content.content:
1:# Engine card — only what a design decision depends on
13:## 1. `is_repeatable` defaults to TRUE when the key is absent
26:## 2. Conditions **fail open** without `version = "1.0"`
55:## 3. Effects say `trait`. Conditions say `trait_key`.
60:# CONDITION
63:# EFFECT
78:# round(charm × mult + add), held inside min / max; mult 1 and add 0 by default
92:## 4. Meter ceilings live in `sidebar_items[].bands[]`
108:## 5. Media: a fixed file, or a folder that cycles
135:## 6. Schedules, and overnight windows
158:## 7. Random events have a per-location cooldown
172:## 8. Linking between canvases
199:### A node link SWAPS the screen. A cascade beat APPENDS to it.
244:## 9. Narration person is per-game and immutable
255:## 10. The location graph — children forward, "Leave X" back
284:## 11. Validator rules that will stop a build
296:## 12. The Start passage is an age gate, not the game
311:## 13. Exit blocks use SECTION syntax, not nested inline tables
332:# a location exit
349:## 14. The third key asymmetry — `npc_id` vs `npcId`
363:## 15. A pure number lock prints its own need; a story lock needs `locked_text`, which REPLACES the label
396:### ⚠️ That is what a shown row must SAY. It is not how many rows to show.
424:## 16. A flag read by a TRIGGER **or a CHOICE** must be set from a LOCATED canvas
482:## 17. The wardrobe — and the most dangerous failure class in this engine
547:### Where a state is read
575:### One thing the wardrobe cannot do, recorded deliberately
587:### Known gaps — the shop
597:## 18. Build
619:## 19. ONE repeatable canvas per location + NPC + time window
653:## 20. `npc_at_location` — cross-room occupancy, and the any-NPC form
675:## 21. `clamp` is 0–100, it defaults to TRUE, and it will silently cap a CURRENCY
705:### ⚠️ 21b. `op = "subtract"` IS NOT AN ENGINE OP. It does nothing at all.
740:## 22. Locations do more than `entry_from` — four fields nobody used
866:## 23. The guidance page — `[[quest_cards]]`, and it is OFF by default in practice
950:# climb  - the goal frame, with live progress
954:# ready  - the Ready frame. NO goals: an empty goals list is allMet vacuously true
959:# done   - the tick, and it means it
992:### The next STEP in the rail — `[[sidebar_items]] type = "quest_next"`
1023:## 24. Reading a built game from outside — four facts that each FAKE A BROKEN GAME
1034:### 24.1 `State`, `Engine` and `setup` hang off `window.SugarCube`
1046:### 24.2 `time_state.current_day` is a day NAME, not an index
1059:### 24.3 Ask the engine who is present — do not recompute it
1071:### 24.4 The built page is ENTITY-ENCODED — macros are not stored literally
1083:## Unverified — do not cite until read
1096:## 25. A speaking block with no `speaker` renders under a placeholder name, not a person
1133:### The three forms, all required to carry `props`
1161:## 26. `[settings.rent]` — the engine charges the money, so do not author a canvas that does
1221:## 27. `costs` on a choice — the only price the engine enforces by itself
1265:## 28. `[engine.daily_tick]` — the day-rollover hook, and the only clean way to day-cap a triggerless rung
1293:### 28.1 The flag goes on the CHOICE, because a choice and an exit run in opposite orders
1314:### 28.2 Two of the three parts validates and does nothing
1325:### 28.3 What the screen looks like once the cap IS spent
1368:## 29. `cap` on an effect — a VALUE ceiling, not a rate limit

## 6. Schedules, and overnight windows

```toml
[[npcs.schedules]]
location = "…"; weekdays = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6]; start_time = "22:00"; end_time = "04:00"; activity = "…"
```

**Wrapping past midnight is supported.** From `setup.isCurrentTimeSlot` in `v2.py`:

```js
// Handle overnight (e.g., 22:00-06:00)
if (endTotal < startTotal) return currentTotal >= startTotal || currentTotal < endTotal;
```

Call sites: `v2.py:4150`, `:4168`, `:4326`. An omitted `end_time` defaults to start + 60 min
(same function).

⚠️ An older note in our own memory claims a window cannot cross midnight and needs two rows.
The source above contradicts it. Either the engine was fixed or the original observation was
about a different path — **verify live before splitting a window.**

---

## 19. ONE repeatable canvas per location + NPC + time window

Two repeatable canvases that bind the same NPC at the same location with overlapping schedules
are a build-time warning, and only one of them will ever render:

```
⚠️  Repeatable canvases 'hub_tom_late' and 'shift_change_frontroom' both trigger for NPC
    'npc_tom' at location 'the_front_room' with overlapping schedules. Only one repeatable
    canvas is allowed per location + NPC + time window. Put multiple interactions inside a
    single canvas as choices instead.
```

It does not stop the build, and it is a note, not an error: the highest `priority` wins (§42, "One
location shows ONE canvas per character"). A canvas shadowed this way is unreachable while the other's
conditions hold, so set the priorities on purpose.

**The fix for THIS collision** — two canvases fighting over the same NPC in the same window — is
the engine's own advice: make the second canvas a triggerless rung and hang it off the existing
hub as a CHOICE. Conditions on a choice are evaluated live at render, so a rung can still be
time-limited and state-limited without owning a schedule of its own — see §20 for the predicate
that makes this worth doing.

⚠️ **THAT ADVICE IS SCOPED TO THIS COLLISION. IT IS NOT A GENERAL DESIGN PREFERENCE.** Read as
one, it turns every location into one paragraph and a wall of buttons, and a hub that binds no NPC
is not covered by §19 at all.

The rule is: *same NPC, same location, overlapping windows.* Two repeatable canvases at one
location that bind **different** NPCs, or **no** NPC, do not collide and **should be separate
canvases** — that is the normal shape, not a workaround. What lives on which screen is
`references/the-surfaces.md`; a room's list is **needs + systems + people** and its length falls out of
that closed set (R2), and **8 is a backstop, not a size** (gate 20 — never treat it as a target).

---

## 42. `trigger.npc` — the portrait, and the presence gate it carries

One key decides whether a character surface is a **face on the location screen** or a **line of link
text**, and the same key is what enforces that character's hours. It lives at the top level of
`[canvases.trigger]`.

```
[[canvases]] npc = …            → dropped. TemplateCanvas has no such field
                                  (template_import.py:1107-1114, built named-only at :2845-2853)

[canvases.trigger] npc = …      → TemplateTrigger.npc (template_import.py:796)
                                  → game_graph.py:344  "npc" into trigger metadata
                                  → v2.py:13265        read back out
                                  → v2.py:13340        "npcId": npc_id,  # NPC slug for navigation portrait indicators
```

**With `npcId`** — `selectNpcPortraitCanvasesForLocation` (`v2.py:5549`) and `renderNpcPortraits`
(`v2.py:6092`) claim the canvas. The renderer then applies the only real presence check in the
engine: the character must have a declared `[[npcs.schedules]]` and `getNpcLocation` must put them
where the player is standing right now (`v2.py:6155-6158`). It draws the portrait and prints
`$npcs[…].name`.

**Without it** — `renderSoloActivities` does not skip the canvas (`v2.py:6238` skips only canvases
that *have* an `npcId`), so it renders as an ordinary activity button carrying the canvas's own
`displayName` (`v2.py:6269`). No face, **no presence check at all**, and the author-facing title
becomes player-facing text. `requires_npc` does not cover the gap unless it is set — §31 above lists
every site that reads it.

⚠️ **One location shows ONE canvas per character.** The renderer gathers every valid repeatable
canvas per NPC and keeps the highest `priority`, preferring affordable over cost-blocked
(`v2.py:6099-6136`). Three Mark surfaces in one kitchen render as one Mark, not three rows. Set the
priorities deliberately: an escalation at 7 above a hub at 6 replaces the hub whenever its conditions
hold, which is usually what you want and is never what you get by accident.

⚠️ **A non-repeatable canvas renders no portrait either** (`v2.py:5557` skips
`!c.isRepeatable`), which is what keeps a meeting from leaking onto the screen as a face — see
`the-first-hour.md` F5b.

**What the misplacement costs.** `npc` written on `[[canvases]]` instead of `[canvases.trigger]`
is discarded: every such entry in the built `help_data.locationCanvases` carries `npcId: null` and
`canvasIdToNpcUuid` is `{}` — no portraits, ungated surfaces, and `Sit with @npc` as a link label.
The build stays green, and the gate that checks hubs (`every hub is met first`) starts by counting
portrait hubs, finds none, and reports **n/a**. The gate `no canvas key is discarded` exists so
that cannot recur. It covers every canvas key, not `npc` alone: `substitution_only` written one
level too high renders a walk-in as a clickable activity instead of a dispatcher-only target.

---

653	## 20. `npc_at_location` — cross-room occupancy, and the any-NPC form
654	
655	```toml
656	{ type = "npc_at_location", location_id = "the_front_room", npc_id = "npc_mark", operator = "is_present" }
657	{ type = "npc_at_location", location_id = "the_front_room", operator = "is_present" }   # ← any NPC
658	```
659	
660	`generators/v2.py:5084-5098` (the runtime branch) and `:9060` (the human-readable dispatcher).
661	`operator` is `is_present` | `is_absent`; `location_id` accepts a slug or a UUID. **`npc_id` is
662	optional — omit it and the test becomes "is this room occupied by anybody".**
663	
664	Verified live in a built game, not just read: a choice carrying
665	`npc_at_location(the_front_room, npc_mark, is_present)` rendered at 23:10, when Mark's

## 20. `npc_at_location` — cross-room occupancy, and the any-NPC form

```toml
{ type = "npc_at_location", location_id = "the_front_room", npc_id = "npc_mark", operator = "is_present" }
{ type = "npc_at_location", location_id = "the_front_room", operator = "is_present" }   # ← any NPC
```

`generators/v2.py:5084-5098` (the runtime branch) and `:9060` (the human-readable dispatcher).
`operator` is `is_present` | `is_absent`; `location_id` accepts a slug or a UUID. **`npc_id` is
optional — omit it and the test becomes "is this room occupied by anybody".**

Verified live in a built game, not just read: a choice carrying
`npc_at_location(the_front_room, npc_mark, is_present)` rendered at 23:10, when Mark's
20:00–23:30 row and Tom's 23:00–01:30 row overlap, and was gone at 23:45 with the same state
and the same player. This is the primitive that makes two-NPC scenes possible at all, since
`requires_npc` binds exactly one.

The any-NPC form has a second use: a scene about being *seen* without specifying who by. No NPC
is bound, so nothing can be mis-attributed — there is no character in scope to attribute to.

# =============================================================================
# Billable Hours — 0 · systems spec
# [project] [settings] [time] [engine] [ui] [player_portrait] [traits] [[sidebar_items]] [[clothing]]
# Built from the signed sheets (sheets/, DECISIONS.md) and the ledger (v2_state.json).
# =============================================================================

[project]
id              = "billable_hours"
title           = "Billable Hours"
description     = "Emma, 21, starts an internship at the law firm where her stepfather is a partner. He paid off her card, and every Friday he takes $250 of her week. Her mother is his assistant. Her step-brother is an associate there and says she didn't earn the job. The house runs on who is in the next room; the firm runs on what she wants."
starting_canvas = "opening_boot"
version         = "0.1"
release_date    = "2026-10-01"
quests_engine   = "v2"

[settings]
narration_person  = "second"
clothing_enabled  = true
wardrobe_location = "her_room"

# The engine collects the bill (engine.md §26). No authored scene takes the money.
[settings.rent]
enabled          = true
amount           = 250
due_day          = "Friday"
collector_npc    = "npc_martin"
start_after_flag = "firm_day1_done"
stages      = [ { amount = 250, after_total_paid = 0 }, { amount = 300, after_total_paid = 500 }, { amount = 350, after_total_paid = 1400 } ]
stage_lines = [
  "Martin folds the envelope into his jacket without counting it. \"Two-fifty. Every Friday, Emma.\"",
  "Martin counts it this time. \"Your mother's card was in your name too. Three hundred from next Friday.\"",
  "\"Three-fifty,\" Martin says, and puts the envelope away. \"That's the last number, Emma. It stays there.\"",
]
on_short         = "carry"
currency_symbol  = "$"

[settings.rent.text]
title         = "Friday"
scene         = "It's Friday. Martin is at the kitchen table with his coffee, and there's an empty space on the table in front of him where the envelope goes."
greeting      = "\"Friday, Emma.\" He doesn't look up from the paper."
paid_scene    = "You put the envelope down. He slides it over with two fingers and it's gone into his jacket."
paid_response = "\"Good girl.\" Your mother smiles at the stove like she didn't hear it."
paid_closing  = "Go to work."
cant_pay      = "You don't have it. He looks at you over the paper for a long time. \"Then it's owed. Next Friday it's all of it.\""
partial_pay   = "He counts what you've got and puts it away. \"The rest next week, Emma. I keep track.\""

[time]
enabled       = true
starting_hour = 7
starting_day  = "Monday"
starting_week = 1

# Day caps: each flag is set on the choice that spends it and cleared here (engine.md §28).
[engine.daily_tick]
flagEffects = [
  { targetType = "player", flag = "worked_today",    op = "unset" },
  { targetType = "player", flag = "breakfast_today", op = "unset" },
  { targetType = "player", flag = "shower_today",    op = "unset" },
  { targetType = "player", flag = "touch_today",     op = "unset" },
  { targetType = "player", flag = "club_today",      op = "unset" },
  { targetType = "player", flag = "drink_today",     op = "unset" },
  { targetType = "player", flag = "eat_today",       op = "unset" },
  { targetType = "player", flag = "dinner_today",    op = "unset" },
]
